item.title: Installing authn-revokd
item.description:
The repository ships three units and an account in packaging/: authn-revokd.service (the daemon), authn-revokd-once.service with authn-revokd-once.timer (the alternative), and sysusers.d/authn-revokd.conf.

path what owner, mode
/usr/local/bin/authn-revokd the binary root, 0755
/usr/lib/sysusers.d/authn-revokd.conf the authn-revokd system account root, 0644
/etc/systemd/system/authn-revokd.service the daemon root, 0644
/etc/authn-revokd/revokd.hcl the configuration, the default -config root, 0644
/etc/authn-revokd/ca/ the CA keys and certificates the lists must be signed by root, 0755; the files in it 0644
/var/lib/authn-revokd/ StateDirectory=, the only writable place authn-revokd, 0755
/var/lib/authn-revokd/state/ state_dir: the verified copies authn-revokd, 0700
/var/lib/authn-revokd/sshd.krl an output: what sshd reads authn-revokd, 0644

Write the outputs to /var/lib/authn-revokd, and point the servers there. An output is written beside its final name and renamed over it, so its directory must be writable. Making /etc/ssh writable would let the authn-revokd account replace sshd_config. Outputs are 0644, chmod-ed explicitly despite UMask=0077, so that sshd and a TLS server running as its own user can read them; the state stays 0700.

The binary, the account, the unit

A release carries authn-revokd-<os>-<arch> for Linux, macOS and Windows on amd64 and arm64, with SHA256SUMS and build provenance (verifying a download). Or go install github.com/go-authn/revocation/cmd/authn-revokd@v0.6.4.

The account and the unit come from the packaging/ directory of the release tag, the same version as the binary: copy that directory beside the binary, from a checkout of the tag or, for v0.6.4, from https://github.com/go-authn/revocation/tree/v0.6.4/packaging.

install -m 0755 authn-revokd-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/authn-revokd
install -m 0644 packaging/sysusers.d/authn-revokd.conf /usr/lib/sysusers.d/authn-revokd.conf
systemd-sysusers /usr/lib/sysusers.d/authn-revokd.conf
install -m 0644 packaging/systemd/authn-revokd.service /etc/systemd/system/
systemctl daemon-reload

The account is static, not DynamicUser=. authn-revokd refuses a state directory owned by anyone but its own uid or root, and the state must keep ordering the next list across restarts and upgrades. With a dynamic user the files would sit under /var/lib/private, 0700 root, and a TLS server running as its own user could not read the CRL.

The daemon 

[Service]
Type=exec
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/authn-revokd -config /etc/authn-revokd/revokd.hcl
ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
Restart=always

and around it: User=authn-revokd, no capability at all, NoNewPrivileges=, ProtectSystem=strict with StateDirectory=authn-revokd (0755) the one writable place, PrivateUsers=, PrivateTmp=, PrivateDevices=, PrivateIPC=, AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_UNIX only, @system-service system calls minus @privileged @resources.

Restart=always, because sshd ignores the expiry in the KRL. The file is failed closed by this process when a list lapses. While it is stopped, sshd keeps reading the last file it wrote, and a revocation issued meanwhile never arrives. Monitor the unit, or /healthz when the mirror is on.

systemctl reload syncs now. It sends SIGHUP, and the agent fetches every source at once instead of at the next refresh:

hangup: syncing now

It does not re-read the configuration, which is read once, at start: after changing revokd.hcl, systemctl restart authn-revokd. (Before v0.6.0 an uncaught SIGHUP killed the process, and systemd counts that as a clean exit.)

Enable it BEFORE wiring sshd

sshd refuses every certificate when RevokedKeys names a file that does not exist

So start authn-revokd first, and wait until the output is there: ssh-keygen -Q -l -f /var/lib/authn-revokd/sshd.krl prints its comment, authn-revokd sshd while every source is current.

systemctl enable --now authn-revokd
journalctl -u authn-revokd -n 20 # "<source>: version N, issued ..., expires ..."
 # "output sshd: wrote /var/lib/authn-revokd/sshd.krl"

Then, in /etc/ssh/sshd_config:

TrustedUserCAKeys /etc/ssh/ca/univ-a-ssh.pub
RevokedKeys /var/lib/authn-revokd/sshd.krl

and sshd -t && systemctl reload ssh. sshd reads RevokedKeys at every authentication, so it needs no reload when authn-revokd rewrites the file: the atomic rename is enough.

A TLS server’s CRL 

ssl_client_certificate /etc/authn-revokd/ca/univ-a-x509.pem;
ssl_verify_client on;
ssl_crl /var/lib/authn-revokd/univ-a.crl; # format = "pem"

A TLS server reads its CRL when it loads its configuration, so it must be reloaded when the file changes. An on_change command runs as the authn-revokd account, which cannot systemctl reload nginx: let systemd watch the file instead, as root, with a path unit (PathChanged= on the output) that starts a oneshot running systemctl reload nginx.

Or: -once, on a timer

authn-revokd -once syncs once and exits, 1 when a list is not current or could not be fetched (what -once reports). The outputs are written either way, and failed closed for sshd once a list lapses.

# authn-revokd-once.service
[Unit]
Conflicts=authn-revokd.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/authn-revokd -config /etc/authn-revokd/revokd.hcl -once
TimeoutStartSec=5min
# authn-revokd-once.timer
[Unit]
Conflicts=authn-revokd.service

[Timer]
OnBootSec=30s
OnUnitActiveSec=1min
AccuracySec=5s
RandomizedDelaySec=10s

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

The one-shot has the daemon’s account and hardening. TimeoutStartSec=5min keeps a sync that hangs on a source from outliving the next tick, and RandomizedDelaySec=10s keeps a fleet started together from polling its issuer in step.

install -m 0644 authn-revokd-once.service authn-revokd-once.timer /etc/systemd/system/
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl disable --now authn-revokd
systemctl enable --now authn-revokd-once.timer

Never enable both: the units conflict, so starting one stops the other. The daemon remains the better choice. It fails a lapsed list closed at its next refresh, where the timer waits for its next tick, and only the daemon serves as a mirror: listen is ignored with -once. A timer that stops firing is a daemon that stopped, so monitor systemctl status authn-revokd-once.

Upgrading, and going back

Install the new binary beside the old, swap, restart. The state carries over: the verified copies keep ordering the next lists, so neither an upgrade nor a rollback to an older binary lets an older list in.

Uninstalling

Remove RevokedKeys and ssl_crl from the servers’ configuration first, and reload them: sshd refuses every certificate once the file is gone.

item.title: The configuration
item.description:
One file, /etc/authn-revokd/revokd.hcl by default (-config names another). It is read once, at start.

state_dir = "/var/lib/authn-revokd/state" # the verified copies: what orders the next list
refresh = "1m"

source "univ-a-ssh" {
 url = "https://login.univ-a.example/ssh/krl" # and .../ssh/krl.sig beside it
 ssh_ca = "/etc/authn-revokd/ca/univ-a-ssh.pub" # what the list must be signed by
}
source "univ-b-ssh" {
 url = "http://mirror.cluster.local:8080/univ-b-ssh" # a mirror: plain http is fine
 ssh_ca = "/etc/authn-revokd/ca/univ-b-ssh.pub"
}
source "univ-a-x509" {
 url = "https://login.univ-a.example/x509/crl"
 x509_ca = "/etc/authn-revokd/ca/univ-a-x509.pem"
}

output "sshd" { # sshd_config: RevokedKeys /var/lib/authn-revokd/sshd.krl
 path = "/var/lib/authn-revokd/sshd.krl"
 sources = ["univ-a-ssh", "univ-b-ssh"] # merged into one file
}
output "tls" { # nginx: ssl_crl /var/lib/authn-revokd/univ-a.crl
 path = "/var/lib/authn-revokd/univ-a.crl"
 sources = ["univ-a-x509"]
 format = "pem"
}

# listen = "127.0.0.1:8080" # serve the verified lists: a mirror

The keys

key default
state_dir required, absolute; created 0700 if missing
refresh 1m how often every source is fetched, a second or more; each wait varies by a tenth either way, so a fleet does not stay in step
listen host:port: serve the verified lists, a mirror; ignored with -once

source "<name>": one list. The name is letters, digits, ., _ and -, not starting with a dot, at most 64 characters: it names a file in the state directory and a path of the mirror.

key
url https://, http:// or file://; a KRL’s signature is fetched from the same URL with .sig appended
ssh_ca the SSH CA’s public key, one authorized_keys line: a KRL source. A certificate is refused here
x509_ca the CA’s PEM certificate: a CRL source
max_age also refuse a list issued longer ago than this, besides its own expiry; refused on a source that feeds a CRL output
revoke_keys let this source’s list revoke plain keys in an output shared with other sources; KRL sources only

output "<name>": one file a server reads.

key
path absolute; written beside itself and renamed over
sources KRL sources, merged into one file; or exactly one CRL source
format der (the default) or pem; CRL outputs only
on_change a command and its arguments, run after the file changes, and again at every sync until it succeeds

One KRL for several CAs

RevokedKeys takes a single file before OpenSSH 10.3, so the KRL sources of an output are merged, and each list keeps its full effect on its own CA, and none on another:

  • Kept: its serials and key IDs, its sections that name no CA (scoped to its own), and its own CA key, which revokes all its certificates.
  • Left out, and logged: another CA’s section, and another CA’s key.
  • Plain user keys are left out when the output has more than one source, unless the source has revoke_keys = true. A KRL cannot scope a key to one CA: sshd checks a certificate’s own key against the file whoever signed it, so a key one CA names would lock its holder out under every CA of the file. An output with one source keeps them.

Each list is first merged alone. One that cannot be merged fails closed for its own CA only; the merged file expires with the first of its current inputs, so a reader that checks expiry sees authn-revokd stop.

The mirror

With listen, authn-revokd serves what it holds, from memory, never from the files a write may be half way through:
GET /<source> the list, with an ETag; If-None-Match answers 304
GET /<source>.sig a KRL’s signature; If-Match on another ETag answers 412
GET /healthz 200 ok, or 503 naming each source with no current list and each output that failed 
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:28474/healthz
ok
$ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:28474/bridge-ssh
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: max-age=30
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
Etag: "83278365ecb0f44b05170bb12f151756"
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:51:05 GMT
Content-Length: 130
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H 'If-Match: "stale"' http://127.0.0.1:28474/bridge-ssh.sig
412

A CRL source has no .sig (404). Mirrors chain: a mirror’s source can be another mirror, since every list verifies by itself. A slow upstream never blocks the mirror’s answers.

What is refused at start

Each of these exits 2 before anything is fetched:

authn-revokd: v/relative-state.hcl: state_dir "state": an absolute path
authn-revokd: v/refresh.hcl: refresh "500ms": a duration of a second or more
authn-revokd: v/both-ca.hcl: source "bridge-ssh": ssh_ca and x509_ca together: one source is one list
authn-revokd: v/sig-name.hcl: source "bridge-ssh.sig": a name that ends in .sig, or healthz, is a path the mirror already serves
authn-revokd: v/mixed.hcl: output "sshd" mixes KRL and CRL sources
authn-revokd: v/krl-format.hcl: output "sshd": format is for CRL outputs; a KRL is what sshd reads
authn-revokd: v/revoke-keys-crl.hcl: source "bridge-x509": revoke_keys is for a KRL source (ssh_ca): a CRL revokes its own CA's certificates only

So does a configuration that is not there:

$ authn-revokd -config nowhere.hcl -once
authn-revokd: nowhere.hcl: no such file or directory

Before v0.6.2 it was the HCL parser’s message: nowhere.hcl: <nil>: Failed to read file; The configuration file "nowhere.hcl" could not be read.

A CRL output also takes one source (a TLS server reads one CRL per issuer), and a CRL source with max_age is refused, because nothing could enforce it:

authn-revokd: v/crl-maxage.hcl: output "tls": source "bridge-x509" has a max_age, which a CRL output cannot enforce: the TLS server judges a CRL by its nextUpdate alone. Remove max_age, or ask the CA for a closer nextUpdate

A TLS server that loaded a CRL keeps it in memory until its nextUpdate, whatever authn-revokd writes.

The state directory is held to sshd’s StrictModes rule. Whoever can replace or remove its files decides which list comes next, and an emptied state lets a replayed older list in. So it may not be a symbolic link, writable by group or others, or owned by anybody but authn-revokd’s user or root. These exit 1:

authn-revokd: state_dir /tmp/authn/revokd/state-wide is writable by its group or by others (mode -rwxrwxrwx): whoever can write there decides which list comes next
authn-revokd: state_dir /tmp/authn/revokd/state-link is a symbolic link (L---------): whoever owns it decides where the state is; name the directory itself

item.title: authn-revokd
item.description:
OpenSSH has no way to distribute a KRL, and nothing in a KRL says it is stale. sshd reads a file that stopped updating months ago as the current list. authn-revokd closes both gaps for the lists authn-bridge publishes: it fetches each list, keeps it only if it verifies, writes it where sshd or a TLS server reads it, and, when a list lapses, writes one that revokes the CA itself. Pure Go, CGO_ENABLED=0, one binary. These pages describe v0.6.4.

$ go install github.com/go-authn/revocation/cmd/authn-revokd@v0.6.4
$ authn-revokd -version
authn-revokd v0.6.4
$ authn-revokd -help
Usage of authn-revokd:
-config string
the configuration file (default "/etc/authn-revokd/revokd.hcl")
-once
sync once and exit: 1 when a list is not current, or could not be fetched
-version
print the version and exit

-help exits 0; before v0.6.2 it exited 2.

Before v0.6.0 the command was revokd, and read /etc/revokd.hcl by default. Nothing reads that file any more; when it is there and the new default is not, the error names both paths.

What it does, in one run

Against a test authn-bridge on loopback, with a KRL source and a CRL source:

$ authn-revokd -config revokd.hcl -once
bridge-ssh: version 0, issued 2026-10-11T09:50:24Z, expires 2026-10-11T10:50:24Z
bridge-x509: version 1791712224691, issued 2026-10-11T09:50:24Z, expires 2026-10-11T10:50:24Z
output sshd: wrote /tmp/authn/revokd/out/sshd.krl
output tls: wrote /tmp/authn/revokd/out/bridge.crl
$ ssh-keygen -Q -l -f out/sshd.krl
# KRL version 0
# Generated at 20261011T115024
# Comment: authn-revokd sshd

A second run with nothing new prints nothing and exits 0: an output is rewritten only when its content changes.

Why the transport does not matter

Every list authenticates itself: a KRL by a detached SSHSIG signature by the CA’s own key, a CRL by its CA’s signature. Every list says when it stops being current. So a list may come over HTTPS, plain HTTP inside a cluster, a mirror, or a file. The transport decides how fast a change arrives, never whether a forged or stale list is taken.

KRL CRL
authentic SSHSIG by the SSH CA key, namespace krl@go-authn.github.io signed by its CA
current expires@go-authn.github.io, which sshd ignores nextUpdate
never backwards krl_version, then generation date CRL Number, then thisUpdate
fail closed authn-revokd writes a KRL that revokes the CA key OpenSSL refuses an expired CRL by itself

Where to go next

Installing it the daemon, or -once on a timer; wiring sshd and nginx
The configuration sources, outputs, the mirror, and what is refused
How a list is verified signature, dates, and never older than the list held, across restarts
When a list lapses the KRL that revokes the CA itself

What it does not do

A revocation reaches a server no faster than authn-revokd polls (refresh), plus the issuer’s delay in issuing again. While the issuer is down, its certificates are refused from the list’s expiry on. Whoever holds a CA’s key can sign any list, as they can sign any certificate.

Licence

BSD-3-Clause.

item.title: How a list is verified
item.description:
A list that does not verify is never written, served or used. The last good copy stays. A fetch that fails, for any reason, never replaces it with an empty answer, which would revoke nothing.

The signature

A KRL is fetched with its signature, <url>.sig: an armored SSHSIG over the whole file, by the SSH CA key configured as ssh_ca, in the namespace krl@go-authn.github.io. The namespace keeps the signature from being taken for anything else. A signer hashes with SHA-512; SHA-256 is accepted too. An RSA signature in the SHA-1 form, which PROTOCOL.sshsig forbids, is refused.

The KRL itself must parse as sshd parses it, and must not carry OpenSSH’s own signature section, which OpenSSH never verifies.

A list signed by any other key is refused:

$ authn-revokd -config revokd-other.hcl -once
bridge-ssh: revocation: the KRL's signature does not verify by SHA256:xm8VDcZUh44N+RQSiPbroPInzkMhN/KCWI/TC+9HPNQ: public key does not match
bridge-x509: version 1791712224691, issued 2026-10-11T09:50:24Z, expires 2026-10-11T10:50:24Z
output sshd: wrote /tmp/authn/revokd/out/other.krl
output tls: wrote /tmp/authn/revokd/out/other.crl
authn-revokd: not current: bridge-ssh

Here ssh_ca named a key that did not sign bridge’s list, and the error names that key. A signature that does not verify may also be a list issued again between the two requests, so both are fetched once more before it is reported. This was the first fetch of that source, so there was no good copy to keep, and the output is the fail-closed list at once. (Before v0.6.2 the same failure carried “the list changed between it and its signature” in front of the message above, as if the list had been issued again.)

The signature is fetched with If-Match: <the list's ETag>. A list issued again between the two requests answers 412, and both are fetched again.

A CRL is checked against the CA certificate configured as x509_ca: its signature first, on the raw bytes, before the rest is parsed, so a large CRL signed by anybody costs a signature check rather than a parse. Then its issuer must be that certificate’s subject; it must have a CRL Number and a nextUpdate after its thisUpdate; and it must not be a delta CRL, nor carry a critical extension other than the CRL Number and the Authority Key Identifier, nor a critical entry extension.

A KRL must also say when it expires, in the expires@go-authn.github.io extension: one that does not could never be told from a stale one.

Bodies are bounded: a KRL at 32 MiB, its signature at 64 KiB, a CRL at 64 MiB.

The dates

A list is current when:

  • now is before its expiry (the KRL’s extension, the CRL’s nextUpdate);
  • it was not issued more than five minutes in the future: an issuer whose clock is ahead by more than that writes lists whose age cannot be known;
  • with max_age, it was issued no longer ago than that.

A list that is not current is refused when fetched. A 304 Not Modified is no news: the copy held may have expired since, and it is judged again at every sync.

Never older than the list held

A list’s position is its version (the KRL’s krl_version, the CRL Number), then its issue time (the KRL’s generation date, the CRL’s thisUpdate). A list may replace the one held only when it has a higher version, or the same version issued later: the same revocations, issued again with a new expiry. Anything else is a rollback: a replayed or restored older list, still signed and unexpired, that would un-revoke what the newer one revoked.

Across restarts too

The list held is kept in state_dir, one file per source holding the list and its signature together, written by a single rename with the directory synced. At start each copy is verified again (expired or not, it orders what comes next), and a copy that no longer verifies is not trusted, not even to order the next one, and is said so in the log.

Here a source is pointed, after a restart, at a list an earlier bridge process served nineteen seconds before, still signed and still unexpired:

$ authn-revokd -config revokd.hcl -once
bridge-ssh: version 0, issued 2026-10-11T09:50:24Z, expires 2026-10-11T10:50:24Z
bridge-x509: version 1791712224691, issued 2026-10-11T09:50:24Z, expires 2026-10-11T10:50:24Z
$ authn-revokd -config revokd-old.hcl -once
bridge-ssh: file:///tmp/authn/revokd/old/bridge.krl: revocation: the list is older than the one held: version 0 issued at 2026-10-11T09:50:05Z, the copy held at 2026-10-11T09:50:24Z
authn-revokd: not fetched: bridge-ssh (the list held is current until 2026-10-11T10:50:24Z)
$ ssh-keygen -Q -l -f out/sshd.krl
# KRL version 0
# Generated at 20261011T115024
# Comment: authn-revokd sshd

The first run wrote no output: the files already held those lists. The older list is refused and the output keeps the newer one. The process that refused it had never seen the newer list: it read it back from state_dir.

Since the state is what makes a rollback detectable, the directory is held to sshd’s StrictModes rule (the configuration). A crash between two writes cannot leave a pair that fails to verify, which would take the rollback guard with it: the list and its signature are one file.

What -once reports

-once exits 1 when a source has no current list, when its last fetch failed, or when an output could not be written, and its last line says which of the first two it is:

last line the source its outputs
not current: <source> holds no current list: never fetched, expired, or past max_age failed closed for sshd
not fetched: <source> (the list held is current until <T>) its fetch failed, but the copy held is still current written from that copy, unchanged, until T

Here the issuer is stopped while both lists held are still current:

$ authn-revokd -config revokd.hcl -once
bridge-ssh: revocation: Get "http://127.0.0.1:28473/ssh/krl": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:28473: connect: connection refused
bridge-x509: revocation: Get "http://127.0.0.1:28473/x509/crl": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:28473: connect: connection refused
authn-revokd: not fetched: bridge-ssh (the list held is current until 2026-10-11T10:50:24Z), bridge-x509 (the list held is current until 2026-10-11T10:50:24Z)

That run left sshd.krl as it was. Once a list held lapses, the same source is reported not current, and both kinds can share the line, as on when a list lapses. Before v0.6.2 both cases were reported not current, which said a list had lapsed when only its fetch had failed; the exit status was 1 then too.

The mirror’s /healthz judges by the copy held instead, and answered ok while the issuer was down and the copies still current.

item.title: When a list lapses
item.description:
A revocation check that lets everything through when the list cannot be had is the one an attacker who can block the list defeats. So when authn-revokd holds no current list from a source, what that source’s list protects is refused, until a current list arrives again.

output while a source has no current list
a KRL, for sshd authn-revokd writes a KRL that revokes the source’s CA key
a CRL, for a TLS server the expired CRL is left in place; OpenSSL refuses an expired CRL by itself

For sshd: revoking the CA itself

sshd has no notion of a list’s expiry: it would go on reading the last file written for ever. But it checks the CA key of every certificate against RevokedKeys. So, in place of the list it cannot vouch for, authn-revokd puts the CA’s own key into the output, and every certificate that CA signed is refused, and nothing else.

Here the issuer is stopped, and the KRL source has max_age = "30s", so the copy held lapses within a minute instead of an hour. The CRL source has no max_age, and its copy is still current:

$ authn-revokd -config revokd-maxage.hcl -once
bridge-ssh: revocation: Get "http://127.0.0.1:28473/ssh/krl": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:28473: connect: connection refused
bridge-x509: revocation: Get "http://127.0.0.1:28473/x509/crl": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:28473: connect: connection refused
output sshd: wrote /tmp/authn/revokd/out/sshd.krl
authn-revokd: not current: bridge-ssh; not fetched: bridge-x509 (the list held is current until 2026-10-11T10:50:24Z)
$ ssh-keygen -Q -l -f out/sshd.krl
# KRL version 0
# Generated at 19700101T010000
# Comment: authn-revokd sshd: FAIL CLOSED, every certificate refused from bridge-ssh
hash: SHA256:Fpa/Ku2Wv1EDCR+KSsqZ2eECTM1zftiBWj01Lr+NO2Q # ssh-ed25519
$ ssh-keygen -Q -f out/sshd.krl ca-ssh.pub
ca-ssh.pub (go-authn/bridge SSH CA): REVOKED

bridge-ssh is not current, and its output is failed closed; bridge-x509 is only not fetched, and its CRL is left as it was (what -once reports). SHA256:Fpa/... is the bridge’s SSH CA. A certificate it signed is now revoked as far as anything reading the file is concerned. The commands above ran in the revokd directory, where out/ is; this one runs beside it, in the directory that holds the test certificates, as on sshcert-authorize’s page, so the same file is ../revokd/out/sshd.krl:

$ ssh-keygen -Q -f ../revokd/out/sshd.krl alice-cert.pub
alice-cert.pub (alice): REVOKED

The comment says FAIL CLOSED and names the source, so a person reading ssh-keygen -Q -l sees why. The file’s date is 1970 when every source has lapsed. The output is written as soon as a sync notices, which for the daemon is its next refresh and for the timer its next tick. When a current list arrives again, the next sync writes it in place of the CA’s key, and the CA’s certificates are accepted again.

The same happens before the first list: a source never fetched has nothing current, and its CA is revoked from the first write. A new installation refuses the CA’s certificates until its first list verifies, rather than accepting them unchecked.

Each CA for itself

In an output that merges several sources, only the lapsed source’s CA is revoked. The others keep their lists. A list that cannot be merged (past the serial ranges go-authn/krl keeps) fails closed for its own CA only, and /healthz names it. Only if the lists merge alone but not together is every CA of the output revoked, and the comment says so (FAIL CLOSED, the output could not be rendered). Keeping the old file instead would let a later lapse go unseen.

For a TLS server: the CRL itself

A CRL already says when it stops being current, and OpenSSL refuses one past its nextUpdate (“CRL has expired”). So authn-revokd leaves the last verified CRL in place, and the TLS server fails closed by itself. That is also why max_age is refused on a source that feeds a CRL output: a server that loaded the CRL keeps it until its nextUpdate, whatever authn-revokd writes.

Readers that check the expiry themselves

The merged KRL carries an expiry, the first of its current inputs’. A reader that checks it, such as go-fileshare’s ssh_krl_file or sshcert-authorize --krl, sees authn-revokd stop as it would see the issuer stop.

This only works while authn-revokd runs

The file is failed closed by authn-revokd. While it is stopped, sshd keeps reading the last file written, current or not. Hence Restart=always on the daemon, and monitoring the unit, or the timer, or /healthz.
